questions.prompt: What is the core move in the inner-front strategy as taught here?
choices: Amplify contradictions already inside the target instead of relying on frontal attack
Attack as publicly as possible to weaken morale
Avoid every conflict that involves factions

explanation.gentle: The chapter defines the move through internal contradiction rather than direct force.
explanation.direct: Start with the mechanism: the strategy works on fault lines already inside the target.
explanation.competitive: The play is to let their own cracks do damage instead of welding them together with your attack.

questions.prompt: Why can direct attack fail against a divided opponent?
choices: It always looks too emotional
It can create forced cohesion around a common enemy
It makes fault lines easier to see

explanation.gentle: The problem is that outside pressure can temporarily simplify internal politics.
explanation.direct: Notice the reversal: attack may unify factions that would otherwise keep pulling against each other.
explanation.competitive: A loud hit can turn a cracked enemy into one camp fast.

questions.prompt: Where does the chapter place the ethical line?
choices: At any attempt to exploit disagreement
Only at public attack
When the operator invents fracture through false suspicion or deception instead of exposing real contradiction

explanation.gentle: The line appears when the operator stops reading instability and starts manufacturing it.
explanation.direct: Mark the boundary here: fabricated mistrust changes the strategy from diagnosis into corrosive subversion.
explanation.competitive: The dirty turn begins when you have to fake the crack.

questions.prompt: Sorin keeps seeing a rival bloc unify after each hard push. What is the strongest adjustment?
choices: Increase the pressure so the bloc has no time to respond
Stop the frontal pressure and study which internal contradictions are real
Switch to louder public criticism

explanation.gentle: He needs diagnosis more than intensity.
explanation.direct: Change the pattern: remove the outside threat that is creating cohesion and test the target's real fault lines.
explanation.competitive: Back off the free glue and make the enemy live with its own split.

questions.prompt: Anwen hears praise for internal destabilization in general. What should she test first?
choices: Whether the target deserves to lose
Whether the contradiction is real or being manufactured through false suspicion
Whether the tactic looks sophisticated

explanation.gentle: She is testing reality, not cleverness.
explanation.direct: Check the source of the fracture: if deception is needed to sustain it, the tactic has crossed the line.
explanation.competitive: Ask whether the crack exists or whether someone is painting it on.

questions.prompt: Bastien sees a coalition that may be split by incentives. What is the best immediate move?
choices: Launch a public attack to force a reaction
Verify the fault line and avoid the move that would give the coalition a common enemy
Leak a false rumor to speed up collapse

explanation.gentle: He should test the crack before trying to use it.
explanation.direct: Confirm the split, then remove the unifying pressure rather than inserting more of it.
explanation.competitive: Read the fracture map first and do not hammer it shut yourself.

questions.prompt: Nabila could widen an old family grievance to win an argument. Which response fits the chapter?
choices: Use the tactic because the fracture already exists
Refuse the tactic because the context is not a proper opponent relationship
Escalate quietly so the others cannot trace it back

explanation.gentle: The framework has context limits, not just technique limits.
explanation.direct: This is a misuse case: inner-front tactics do not belong in ordinary relationships that need clarification or withdrawal instead.
explanation.competitive: Do not treat the family room like enemy territory just because the leverage is there.

questions.prompt: Jorah wants to surface a real factional disagreement in a student committee. What is the strongest test?
choices: Whether naming the issue clarifies reality without inventing extra suspicion
Whether the disagreement can be used to embarrass the other side
Whether the room will remember who raised it

explanation.gentle: The question is whether he is revealing or engineering.
explanation.direct: Use the clarity test: surface the actual contradiction without adding fabricated mistrust to widen it.
explanation.competitive: Expose the real crack and keep your hands off the poison kit.

questions.prompt: When is this strategy most legitimate?
choices: When the target contains real contradictions and the method does not depend on invented mistrust
When the operator can destabilize any tense group efficiently
When outside pressure is likely to create the biggest public spectacle

explanation.gentle: Legitimacy here depends on reality and limit discipline.
explanation.direct: The narrow clean version works only with genuine fault lines in a real opponent and without fabricated distrust.
explanation.competitive: A real crack plus a clean read can be strategy. Poison-making cannot.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 32 differ from this chapter's mechanism?
choices: It focuses on louder public attack
It shifts from internal fracture inside the target to concealed submission and parallel leverage by the weaker operator
It abandons indirect strategy altogether

explanation.gentle: The next chapter moves from inner contradiction to hidden capacity under outward compliance.
explanation.direct: Chapter 32 changes the mechanism by focusing on seeming to submit while building parallel leverage, not on widening fault lines inside the target.
explanation.competitive: This chapter reads the enemy's cracks. The next one hides your own counterforce under submission.
